evidence: Searched src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Backend/CasProbe.h and CasProbe.cpp for vendor-support wording; the design is vendor-agnostic (runCapabilityProbe + probeConditionalCopy pass/fail on any backend, no AWS/GCP/Azure branching). Searched docs/en/antalya/cas/ for a bucket-requirements page and any 'AWS'/'GCP'/'Azure'/'probably works' wording -- none exists. Only utils/ca-soak/docker-compose-awss3.yml and utils/ca-soak/docker-compose-gcs.yml provide vendor-specific soak test infra; there is no Azure compose file or any explicit vendor-support statement anywhere in the tree. Cannot confirm or deny the specific 'AWS and GCP work, Azure probably works' wording.

Searched src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/ for a namespace-nesting prohibition tied to prefix LIST (none found in ContentAddressedMetadataStorage.cpp/.h or CasLayout.h); actual verbatim-file layout at HEAD is cas/ns/state/<life_id>/_files/... (src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Formats/CasLayout.cpp:172-188, CasLayout.h:243), not '@cas@/_files/' as claimed, and loose mountpoint objects live at roots/<server_root_id>/<path> (ContentAddressedMetadataStorage.cpp:1372,1836), close to but not exactly 'roots/<server>/<path>'. Grepped the whole ContentAddressed tree for '_disk' as a magic namespace token -- zero matches, so cannot confirm it was ever eliminated (or ever existed). The core no-nesting invariant claim could not be located anywhere in code or comments.

src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/ObjectStorages/Local/LocalObjectStorage.cpp:433-499 listObjects: isVanishedEntryError (line 377-380) treats ENOENT/ENOTDIR as a concurrently-vanished entry to be omitted rather than a hard failure, and the traversal uses an explicit std::vector<fs::path> pending_dirs stack of non-recursive fs::directory_iterators (lines 463-491) specifically to avoid the recursive_directory_iterator's silent-drop-of-later-siblings bug on a removed subdirectory. tryGetObjectMetadata (lines 397-431) applies the same tolerance for per-entry stats, citing B38 by name at line 413.

src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Gc/CasGc.h:30-65 UniversePolicy enum: a hidden acked namespace not covered by hint/gc/state cannot be proven by any per-namespace LIST-based probe (comment lines 36-41); kDefault = Authoritative requires the gate to open only on a COMPLETE, CATALOG-PROVEN frontier (lines 51-52), and any failure of that 'suppresses every destructive site POOL-WIDE' (lines 57-59) -- i.e. the pool-wide suppression is the fallback for an incomplete frontier, while the normal reclaim path is per-blob in-degree reaching zero on a complete, catalog-proven frontier (Gc/CasGc.cpp:1818 'in-degree reached 0').

src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Pool/CasRefLedger.h:70-73 lists the exact operation set that shares the ledger's captured runtime: 'the flat-combining append lane and its unresolved-PUT wedge, snapshot publication, stale-precommit cleanup, cache-budget eviction, and remount/shutdown draining'; CasRefLedger.cpp:4277 states 'retirement/remount can invalidate the captured runtime while it [is in use]', and CasRefLedger.cpp:2270/3691/4361 each throw when 'its captured runtime was retired before <wedged-frontier|committed-frontier|checkpoint> publication', confirming the monotone-retirement/remount-supersession check across these call sites.

src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Primitives/CasEvent.h:29 defines CasEventType::GcAnomaly and CasEvent.cpp:46 serializes it to 'gc_anomaly', but a repo-wide grep for GcAnomaly usage (src/**/*.cpp, src/**/*.h) shows it is never emitted anywhere -- only defined and stringified. The actual anomaly bookkeeping is RoundReport::anomalies, an uncapped std::vector<RoundAnomaly> (src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Gc/CasGc.h:143, recordAnomaly at line 158) with no 32-row cap, no 'true total' field, and no truncation log line anywhere in Gc/CasGc.cpp's anomaly-handling code (lines 3068-3116).

Confirmed scratch_bytes is a real sampled metric (utils/ca-soak/scenarios/framework/sampler.py:16,83,104-106) and that CAS has a distinct local scratch-staging cleanup concern (src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/ContentAddressedTransaction.cpp:971 'drop the orphan instead of leaking it into scratch'), but the specific numeric readings (1 MiB->21 MiB on ch1, 16 KiB->21 MiB on ch2 during idle GC) are a one-off soak-run observation not encoded anywhere in code; grepped utils/ca-soak/logs_archive/ for scratch_bytes and found no archived sample data matching these figures, so the exact numbers cannot be confirmed or refuted from the repository.

src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Formats/CasRefCatalogFormat.h:65 states the incarnation-token design 'is what makes rebirth structurally inert instead of an alias', and CasRefCatalog.h:319 notes a same-incarnation-only rebirth rule; this incarnation mechanism closes the rebirth/resurface hazard for every lifecycle state uniformly (not just Live), superseding the narrower 'Live-only sealing, extend to Removed as a follow-up' plan described in the Task-8 rev.6 review finding.

src/Disks/tests/gtest_cas_namespace_janitor.cpp:280 TEST(CASNamespaceJanitor, SuppressionAndFenceLossDeleteNothing) is exactly the missing test the claim describes: it asserts janitor.runOnePage(/*suppress=*/true, ...).deleted == 0, that gc/state gains no progress, and that both seeded objects survive (lines 290-299). The dropped test obligation has since been added.

src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Gc/CasGc.cpp contains explicit 'PHASE n/18' comments for every round phase (e.g. line 500 'PHASE 1/18 lease', line 1776 'PHASE 7/18 fold_seal_read', line 3316 'PHASE 10/18 fold_seal_write', line 1042 'PHASE 13/18 round_commit', line 1237 'PHASE 18/18 orphan_sweep') -- the GC round is an 18-phase split at HEAD, not the 17-phase split the claim describes.

Searched src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Formats/CasFormat.h, CasRecordStreamFormat.h/.cpp, and Pool/CasRefCkpt.cpp/.h for 'footer', 'indexed block', 'base run', and 'non-overlapping key bounds' -- none of that vocabulary or a multi-GET (HEAD + footer-range-GET + indexed-block-range-GET) cold-run read path exists anywhere in the tree. The only checkpoint read path found, CasRefCkpt.cpp:189 readCkpt, is a single whole-object backend.get() with no footer/index-block structure at all.

src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Pool/CasPartWriteTxn.cpp:191-198 PartWriteTxn::uploadBlobDetached: 'HEAD-before-PUT on a likely dedup hit (cache says present) or a large body (... on a store that early-closes a doomed conditional PUT, the broken-pipe and retry storm caused by early rejection)' -- head_first gates on cache_hit or size >= cfg.deduplication_head_first_min_bytes. B187 is documented as the rustfs Expect:100-continue/broken-pipe concern in utils/ca-soak/configs/storage_conf_gc_shards8_ch1.xml:27.

src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Pool/CasRefLedger.h:702-703 RefTableRuntime comment: 'One coherent decoded RefTableState and append runtime for a namespace. It is recovered lazily and evicted only as a whole.' Line 72 confirms the ledger owns 'the recovered whole-table cache ... cache-budget eviction'; line 901 documents the monotonic access stamp used for whole-table LRU eviction.

src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Pool/CasRefProtocol.h:430 declares `RefTableState replay(const std::optional<RefTableSnapshot> & snapshot, std::span<const RefLogTxn> tail);` -- the reader-visible state is the fold of a base snapshot plus the log tail, not the bare newest snapshot, matching the claim's substance (parameter names differ slightly: 'snapshot, tail' rather than 'base_snapshot, log tail').

src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/ContentAddressedMetadataStorage.cpp:1670-1690 listDirectory's ShadowTable/ShadowPart cases resolve part names via store()->listRefs(...) / a PartFolderAccess view, both backed by the ledger's replay()'d RefTableState (Pool/CasRefProtocol.h:430), not a raw object-store LIST; only the unrelated ShadowIntermediate directory-browsing case performs a live mirrored LIST for clickhouse-disks-style path enumeration.

src/Storages/StorageSnapshot.h:20-30: 'Additional data, on which set of columns may depend. E.g. data parts in MergeTree...' held via `DataPtr data` on the StorageSnapshot captured once per query -- this is the generic ClickHouse mechanism by which a running query holds its part set for the query's duration regardless of concurrent storage refreshes; there is no standalone class literally named `DataPart` (it is `MergeTreeData::DataPartPtr = shared_ptr<IMergeTreeDataPart>`).

src/Storages/StorageTableProxy.h:14,43: 'Lazily creates underlying storage for tables in databases with `lazy_load_tables` setting' / LOG_TRACE 'Loading lazy table on first access'. This is the generic ClickHouse lazy-table-load mechanism (not CAS-specific): the nested storage, including its replication queue/merge scheduling, is only constructed via getNested() on first access, matching the claim's substance.

utils/ca-soak/scenarios/cards/s19_s22_clone_fetch.py:169-196: the S19 scenario's own comment explicitly attributes the observed CASRootCompareSwap=2 during the gated cross-disk MOVE PARTITION to 'a concurrent GC round' via lease-gated background GC, not to the move itself, and explicitly instructs 'Do NOT gate on CASRootCompareSwap ... GC round landing inside the move's wall-clock window inflates it with ref-CASes that have nothing to do with the move.' This directly contradicts the claim's causal reading that two CasRootCas operations occurred as part of the move's own (non-atomic) validation path; the actual atomicity proof used is CASBlobPut==0 plus fsck dangling==0. `Code:479 UNKNOWN_DISK` is a real error code (src/Common/ErrorCodes.cpp:392) and is what the scenario expects, but the '2 CasRootCas ops before validation' narrative is refuted by HEAD's own scenario comment.

src/Disks/tests/gtest_cas_protocol_scenarios.cpp:11-27 documents that 'promote refreshes the retire view when the fence is ahead' and that a non-tokened leaf gets 'the single mandatory presence observation' (in-closure revalidation) while tokened leaves are edge-protected and skipped; line 138 comment on the PrematureCondemnDoesNotDangle-style test: 'promote: mutateShard refreshes the view (fence_round 1 > view round 0), but the tokened leaf is edge-protected -- skipped, not re-validated'. This matches the claim's mechanism (a pre-pass at round R, mutateShard refreshing to R', with the revalidation inside the closure being the only thing that observes condemnations in that window), though the literal tokens 'retire-view'/'R\'' are not used verbatim.

Grepped the whole tree (excluding tmp/ and worktree scratch dirs) for 'RunFileReader' -- it appears only inside a single doc comment in src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Backend/CasBackend.h:219 ('RunFileReader bounds to its data_end'), with no class of that name and no seek()/min_key/max_key comparison logic anywhere in the ContentAddressed tree. The only real block-oriented reader found, SourceEdgeRunReader (Formats/CasRecordStreamFormat.h:134), has no seek method or block-boundary key-comparison logic at all. The described bug (last-block-by-min_key selection skipping a duplicated boundary key) and its fix (first-block-by-max_key) are not implemented anywhere at HEAD.

src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Parts/PartFolderAccess.h:58 'getView, which under ForceFresh always re-proves the manifest body (mandatory HEAD ...)' -- the mandatory-GET/HEAD cost is specific to building a materialized folder view via getView; plain existence checks (ContentAddressedMetadataStorage.cpp:1359 existsFile, :1490 existsDirectory) do not go through getView and so do not validate a manifest body.

src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Formats/CasPartManifestFormat.cpp:263-269 enforces strict ascending-order/no-duplicate-path on manifest entries at parse time specifically to keep 'findEntry/entryRange's binary-search precondition (strictly ascending m.entries) sound' (comment at line 262), and findEntry (CasPartManifestFormat.h:113, .cpp:329) performs the binary search -- i.e. O(log n) manifest lookups. The manifest is held as a shared_ptr<const Cas::PartManifest> (PartFolderAccess.h:99,124), so no per-operation copy is made on the read path. Entries out of canonical order are rejected with CORRUPTED_DATA (cpp:265-267).

src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/ContentAddressedSettings.cpp:89 DECLARE(String, part_folder_validate, "always", ...) confirms 'always' is the default. src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Parts/PartFolderAccess.h:58 confirms ForceFresh under this policy issues a mandatory HEAD to re-prove each manifest body, i.e. one S3 HEAD per file validated before a wide part's removal collapses to one ref-drop.

src/Interpreters/DatabaseCatalog.cpp:367 tryGetByUUID reads directly from `uuid_map`, a separate UUID->StoragePtr map independent of the database's table-name map that a database-map-entry swap would update; src/Interpreters/ActionLocksManager.cpp:39-41 ActionLocksManager::add keys action-lock bookkeeping off the StoragePtr obtained via DatabaseCatalog::tryGetTable, i.e. off whichever pointer identity (proxy or real storage) is currently registered. src/Storages/StorageProxy.h:11 defines StorageProxy itself. Together these confirm that swapping only the database-name-map entry leaves the UUID map and action-lock bookkeeping still pointing at the StorageProxy.

The two named mechanisms are real: CachedPartFolderAccess::republishRef (src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Parts/PartFolderAccess.cpp:506) re-proves the source body and republishes it under a fresh incarnation, and PartWriteTxn::promote (src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Pool/CasPartWriteTxn.cpp:1050) fails closed on an invalid/condemned manifest with no retry of its own. Separately, src/Storages/MergeTree/ReplicatedMergeTreeAttachThread.cpp:88 confirms that a failed attach leaves the table readonly with no automatic retry logic visible at that call site. No code was found anywhere in the ContentAddressed or MergeTree/Replication trees that specifically retries an attach after a promote abort caused by a condemned-token race on a ZK-unknown CA part, so the described permanent-readonly gap appears real and unaddressed at HEAD.
